hanna_root.text: Hanna wipes the counter with a rag and sizes you up. "New off the continent. Here they pay first and ask later. What do you need, John?"

options.text: Something hot and a mug of beer.
I'm looking for work. Who pays cash in this town?
Who's at the gaming table today?
I need a bed for the night.
I hear I have a tab with you.
[Intimidate 3] Forget the tab I owe you.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

hanna_meal.text: "Six crowns for a bowl of stew and bread. Beer is two. Don't expect credit — you have a debtor's face."

hanna_work.text: "There's as much work as there's dirt in the alleys. Orlik the smith wants coal — he pays on the spot. Ewa down by the water buys fish. And if your hands are soft and your conscience hard, Idzi hangs around the third pier after dark. I never told you that."

options.text: Orlik, you say. Where do I find him?
Thanks. I'll buy you a round one day.

hanna_idzi.text: "Whatever customs didn't write down. Untaxed salt, untaxed beer, sometimes something that was still in the church yesterday. Listen — if they catch you with his goods, I'll say I've never seen you before. And I'll mean it."

options.text: And how do you know all this?

hanna_secret_hint.text: "Because an inn is the town's ear, John. Everybody says something after the third mug. Now go, my guests are getting cold."

hanna_gossip.text: "Gossip costs, but for a newcomer one is free. The Wild Knights take a cut from every stall. For three days customs officer Bernard has worn a face like he swallowed a lemon — twenty barrels of salt are missing from his books. And the hangman Baltazar is circling the gallows again, which means somebody will swing soon."

options.text: Twenty barrels of salt. Somebody's making a deal.

hanna_gallows.text: "A boy from the suburbs. He took a sack of grain from the customs store because his mother had nothing to pay for a funeral. Baltazar says it's a quarter hour of work. The town says it's a performance."

hanna_dice.text: "By day Cecylia sits at the window — a merchant's widow. Cards, and she hates cheats. After dark Pankracy comes — dice, hot temper, a knife in his boot. I don't open the table for strangers: you have to be let in. And you need a stake in coin, not in promises."

options.text: Introduce me to the table. (5 crowns for the kitchen)

hanna_room.text: "Room upstairs, four crowns a night. Fresh straw, the door has a lock — though a lock here is more decoration than anything. If you want to sleep, go up and lie down."

options.text: I'll take the room tonight. (4 crowns)

hanna_tab.text: "Thirty crowns. I wrote it on the board by the barrel so I wouldn't have to trust my memory. Pay today and your bowl is free. Pay in a week and you'll drink elsewhere."

options.text: I'll dice for it. If I win, the tab is gone.
I'll come when I have it.

hanna_tab_dice.text: "Oh no, darling. I don't play. But Pankracy will, if you meet his stake. Win, and you buy my chit from him and bring it here. That's how adults do it."

hanna_threat.text: Hanna puts the rag down and looks at you for a long time. "I've seen thirty like you in my life. Twenty-nine of them hanged or drank themselves to the bottom of the harbour. Get out before I call Rawicz."

options.text: Forgive me. I'll pay when I can.
Call him. The guard owes me too.

orlik_root.text: Orlik doesn't stop working. He talks over his shoulder, in a voice used to noise: "If you didn't come with iron or with coin, stand aside — sparks fly."

options.text: I'm looking for work with coal.
I want to stand at the anvil.
I hear the guild has trouble with the Knights.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

orlik_coal.text: "Coal. Three baskets. I have next to none and the carts from the quarry have been standing in the rain. Bring me three lumps — sixty-five crowns and permission to touch my anvil. I won't sell you coal cheaper, because then I'd buy it from myself."

options.text: I'll bring three lumps of coal.
Too rich for me. I'll find other work.

orlik_coal_where.text: "Honestly? The quarry cart stands by the west gate, next to the stone heap. The guard watches the cart but doesn't look down. Dishonestly — I didn't ask and you didn't say. And don't bring me wet coal, I won't take it."

options.text: I know as much as I need to.

orlik_teach.text: "Teach? Lad, I have a guild apprentice and I have my schedule. But if your hands know what a hammer is, I'll show you one thing: how not to waste iron. Three days of my time and a hundred thirty crowns for coal and steel. Not less, because the guild audits me."

options.text: Teach me. Three days, a hundred thirty crowns.
I'll learn on my own, at your anvil.
I don't have that much. I'll be back.

orlik_guild.text: "'Trouble' is too small a word. The Knights take every tenth piece 'for protection'. Zbylut at the Guild reckons it will settle down. I reckon how much iron is in my chest. If you want to know who here sides with the Knights — ask at the Guild, not at my forge. I have children."

orlik_sabotage.text: Orlik puts the hammer down. "It could. Only once you do it, there's no going back. Think about whether you want to be the one who sets fires instead of the one who forges. I have a smithy, not an army."

vagn_root.text: Old Vagn leans on a fence post and reads you from boots to hands. "Mercenary. I can tell by how you stand: weight on the left leg, because the right one got hit once. Say what you want, I haven't got all day."

options.text: I want you to teach me.
One round with me. No steel.
I know you from the stories. You fought at Vranov.
Rawicz is moving against the Raven. We need people.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

vagn_teach.text: "Teach a stranger? I taught three. Two are dead, the third drinks. I don't teach for money — I teach for respect, and respect is bought with work. Show me you can stay on your feet when somebody's hitting you. Spar with me in the yard."

vagn_spar.text: Vagn takes a training staff from the rack. "Three hits and we're done. It hurts as usual. Don't count on mercy, count on your legs."

options.text: Wait. Let me warm up first.

vagn_parry.text: "Parrying. Two days in the yard, a hundred twenty crowns — beer for me and salve for you — and one thing: you won't learn it from a book, only from pain. Agreed?"

options.text: Agreed. Two days and a hundred twenty crowns.

vagn_past.text: "A horse. Not mine. At Vranov, in forty-eight. The horse was somebody else's and the leg was mine. I stayed alive because I knew how not to move for three days in a ditch. That's why I teach people to stand, not to swing iron."

options.text: Three days in a ditch. That's a better lesson than ten years of drill.

vagn_vranov.text: "Nobody. That's why they call it a slaughter, not a battle. The Knights who take your cut today are the same ones who burned villages on the way there. Remember that, because one day you'll have to choose a side. And don't choose by money."

idzi_root.text: Idzi stands in the warehouse shadow and doesn't step into the light. "Speak low and don't point. Everybody in the harbour has eyes and half of them are on customs' payroll."

options.text: I want work that pays better than coal.
I have goods to sell. Don't ask where from.
Teach me to walk so nobody sees me.
Bernard is missing twenty barrels of salt in his books.
Where does the Raven keep copies of his ledger?
I need to disappear from the island.
I have six hundred crowns for the passage token.
I did the salt job for you. Now I need to disappear.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

idzi_job.text: "There's an untaxed crate in warehouse A. It has to get to the third pier, in the dark, past the customs man and his lantern. Two hundred forty crowns. If they catch you, I don't know you. If you drop it, I don't know you either. Deal?"

options.text: I'm in. Where's the warehouse key?
And if the guard sees me?
Too risky. I'd rather haul coal.

idzi_key.text: "The key is where it always is: in the lock, on the inside. The yard gate has a lock as old as the harbour — a pick or a strong back. Don't go by day; Bernard has a habit of counting crates in the afternoon."

idzi_risk.text: "Then I'll tell you how law works in this harbour. The guard doesn't know something is gone until somebody tells them. What counts is witnesses, light and noise. See a lantern — stand in shadow and count your breaths. If they catch you with the crate in your hands you have three choices: a fine, the stocks, or running. Running is cheapest but needs legs."

options.text: Then I go in the dark.
Thanks. That's more than anyone ever told me.

idzi_teach.text: "I teach shadow-work for a hundred fifty crowns and two days. But only to people who've already done something for me — otherwise I'm teaching a future witness against myself. Help me once, then we'll talk."

options.text: Teach me now. I have the money.

idzi_salt_known.text: Idzi stops smiling. "Who told you that? ...Never mind. If you know, then you also know half that salt came out of my warehouse. You have two roads now: sell it to Bernard for gratitude, or keep your teeth shut and have me on your side. There's no third."

options.text: Bernard would pay for that news.

idzi_who.text: "I was boatswain on the St Elmo. She went down with somebody else's cargo, and the cargo's owner decided the fault lay with the man who survived. Since then I carry things that aren't in any book. Your question wasn't about me, it was about how much I know. And I know a lot."

rawicz_root.text: Sergeant Rawicz rests a hand on his hilt. "Speak short. I have twelve men, forty drunks and one town that refuses to behave."

options.text: I want to pay the fine and close the matter.
I confess. I'd rather have the stocks than run.
I have news about the salt from the customs warehouse.
What do you take for looking the other way?
I have the Raven's debt ledger. In black and white.
The guild, the Church and the suburb are with us.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

rawicz_fine.text: "The fine goes to the town coffers, not to me. Whatever you're carrying that belongs to somebody else stays in the evidence store. You pay and you're clean — until next time."

rawicz_confess.text: "Confession is half the punishment, but in this town it's the half that costs days. Stocks on the market until dusk, then a night in the guard's cellar. You lose a day, maybe two. But nobody will be looking for you. Choose."

rawicz_bribe.text: "I don't take them. I have a wife and two daughters, and a bribe in this town ends with somebody writing your name in a book. But I know men who do. The guard at the customs gate has debts. Just remember that I don't know about it."

rawicz_why.text: "Because I have twelve men and I need to know which of them is bought. And because you have the face of a man who will end up on the other side sooner or later. I'd rather know early."

rawicz_inform.text: "Say it precisely. Crates, hours, who carried them. If it's true you have my gratitude and twenty crowns from the coffers. If you're lying to settle a rival's account, I'll know, and I'll remember your name."

options.text: It's Idzi. Warehouse A, third pier, after dark.
I won't talk without payment up front.

rawicz_knights.text: "Officially? The town hall and the guild. Unofficially — Baldwin Crow has half the council in his pocket and the other half in fear. I have twelve men with spears against thirty in mail. That's why I watch the market and not the castle. Now go, they're seeing me with you."

teodor_root.text: Father Teodor has host-flour on his hands and eyes that have seen too much. "John. I heard about your debt before you walked into town. Sit, or stand if you prefer — the Lord listens in both positions."

options.text: I'm looking for the relic of Saint Elenem.
Will the Church help me with the debt?
You spoke of Vranov, Father. What should I do about it?
Rawicz is preparing to strike. We need the bells.
I brought back Saint Elenem's reliquary.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

teodor_confess.text: "Confession is free, penance isn't. Say what's on your conscience — theft, blood, lies. I won't write it in a book, but I will remember. That is my job and my punishment."

teodor_killers.text: "How many? ...Don't answer. I'll tell you something I don't say from the pulpit: I remember the fire at Vranov and I remember who lit it. If your debt to the Knights is the price of silence, then it isn't a debt, it's blackmail. And a blackmailer can be acquitted in his own heart. Say three Hail Marys and go do something good."

options.text: How do you know about the fire?

teodor_fire.text: "Because I was there with the last rites. I held a boy's hand, and you stood three steps away watching whether anyone was coming. I'm not accusing. I'm only saying the island is small and people's memory is long."

teodor_nosoul.text: "Everyone says that until they dream of the face of somebody they hurt. Come back when you dream it. The doors are open from dawn and I am more patient than your creditors."

teodor_alms.text: "Three crowns in the box is bread for two families for a day. You won't get a place in heaven for it, but you'll get gratitude at the market, and that's more practical."

options.text: I'll give more when I have it.

teodor_relic.text: "The reliquary of Saint Elenem vanished from the abbey ruins three years ago. The Church says pagans took it. I say someone from the island took it and sold it, because the winter was long. I won't bless a search — but I won't tell the guard either, if the reliquary comes back to the altar."

options.text: If I find it, I'll bring it to you.

teodor_relic_value.text: "Three hundred crowns at Idzi's in the harbour, and four hundred years of somebody's prayer. Choose which price you want to know."

teodor_debt.text: "The Church doesn't pay debts to an armed brotherhood — that would mean we accept their law. I can give you three things: bread, a bed for one night at the almshouse, and a letter to Zbylut of the Guild so he looks on you more kindly. I have nothing more."

options.text: Thank you. That's more than I expected.

teodor_read.text: "Reading is taught by the scribe Urban, not by me — I teach what to do with the reading. Go to him for a notebook and a quill. A man without a notebook remembers only what he wants to remember, and that is the shortest road to being cheated."

marta_root.text: The girl steps back into shadow, appraising you. "Don't come that close. Your hand is on your purse, which means you think you have something worth stealing. What do you want, mercenary?"

options.text: Keep your hands to yourself and we'll both be fine.
They say you're the best in the trade.
I hear somebody took something from you.
I need to get into a locked warehouse.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

marta_respect.text: "Good. First rule: don't watch the hands, watch the hips. Hands lie, hips don't. Second: never work where they know you. Third: don't tell me how to live, because I'm fifteen and I have more corpses in my memory than you have in your ledger."

marta_teach.text: "Best? I'm the only one not sitting in the stocks. I teach for forty crowns and one day. Condition: you don't steal from anyone who has less than you. Break that and I won't hand you in — you'll hand yourself in."

options.text: Forty crowns and a day. Deal.
Principles are a luxury. I can't afford them.

marta_principle.text: "That's exactly why you're thirty-six and in debt instead of having a house. I'm fifteen and I owe nobody anything but myself. Think about that when you sleep on the market."

marta_satchel.text: "Three of them. In the west alley, by the collapsed hut. They took my satchel and in it my mother's savings — eleven crowns and a silver clasp. I won't go there alone, they'd kill me. Will you go? I'll give you the satchel and what's in it, and I'll teach you one thing free."

options.text: Three is too many. I'll come back when I'm ready.
Forget the satchel. I'll teach you not to get robbed twice.

marta_alternative.text: Marta looks at you for a long moment, as if for the first time an adult spoke to her instead of over her. "Fine. But the satchel first. Then we'll talk about principles."

marta_lock.text: "The lock on warehouse A is an old mechanism, four pins. A pick and patience: half a minute. Without a pick — your back and the hinge. But remember: once you open a lock you don't close it, and in the morning somebody will see it and count."

options.text: Knowing the pin count is enough.

goslaw_root.text: Goslaw unrolls a parchment on his stall and holds the corners down with stones. "Cartographer. I sell what I know and I buy what I don't. Plan of the harbour and Lower Town: forty crowns. Drawn from nature, not from rumours."

options.text: I'll buy the town plan. (40 crowns)
Do you have a plan of the whole island?
I have news about the terrain. Will you buy it?
Why are your maps better than others?
Tell me about yourself and this place.

goslaw_island.text: "I do. A hundred eighty crowns and one caveat: half the island on it is drawn from fishermen's stories, so the eastern marshes may be a day's journey further than I've drawn them. You'll buy it anyway, because nobody else has anything."

options.text: I'll take the island plan. (180 crowns)

goslaw_sell_knowledge.text: "I buy. Tell me something that isn't on my parchment: a crossing, a ford, a place the guard doesn't walk, a cave, a well. For true news I pay ten to thirty crowns. For invention I pay nothing and remember your face."

options.text: There's a gap in the customs wall at the eastern end.
I know of a cave under the cliff.

goslaw_craft.text: "Because I walk. Forty years of walking. Others draw from an inn window and then a peasant drowns his cart in a marsh that on their map is a meadow. My map won't save your life, but at least it will lie honestly."

options.text: Lie honestly. That's the most one can ask of a map.

baldwin_root.text: Baldwin Crow stands on the pier in a cloak no harbour could dirty. "John. Thirty-six years old, ten thousand crowns, thirty days. Let's sit like merchants, not like creditor and debtor. It's the same conversation, only politer."

options.text: I'll pay. I just need time.
I want to negotiate an extension.
What happened at Vranov that I'm in your book?
Perhaps I'd be useful to you with a sword.
I have thought about your offer. I am in.
I am back with blood on my sword.
Tell me about yourself and this place.
I won't pay a single crown.

baldwin_time.text: "Time is the one commodity I don't buy. You have thirty days, and every day you don't pay costs you interest — fifty crowns a day past the deadline. Pay in part whenever you like. Gwidon takes payments at the customs gate from dawn to dusk. It's a fairer arrangement than most in this town."

options.text: I'll pay what I have now.
I'll come when I have more.

baldwin_extend.text: "An extension costs. Ten more days for a thousand crowns up front and one favour, chosen by me, at a time chosen by me. The favour won't be bloody — I'm not a butcher, I'm a merchant with a sword. But it may be uncomfortable."

options.text: A thousand crowns and a favour. Agreed.
I don't have a thousand. Let's talk differently.
I don't sell favours sight unseen.

baldwin_vranov.text: Baldwin goes quiet for a moment. "Vranov. A pretty word for an ugly thing. You were there on the other side of the fence, John. That's why your debt has your name on it and not a number. It isn't about ten thousand. It's about making you remember, for thirty days, who you owe for nobody remembering you. Now go and earn."

baldwin_join.text: "You would be. But you don't join the brotherhood with a debt — you join instead of the debt. Eighty days of service: escorts, collection, guard duty. In return the debt vanishes and you get a cloak and a reputation you won't wash off. Think it over, because it's the one thing you can't resell."

options.text: I'll think it over. I'm not saying no.
No. I'll pay the debt with my own hands.

baldwin_refuse.text: "Then we'll meet on the thirtieth day. I won't shout — shouting is for men who have neither right nor money. I'll only say your name in front of witnesses, and then you'll do what people with no way out do. Farewell, John."

collector_root.text: Gwidon Frost has a ledger under his arm and a hand on his hilt. "John. Which day it is, how much is left, how much you paid — in that order. I have no time for stories, I have a list."

options.text: You have no right to stop me.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

collector_status.text: Gwidon opens the ledger and reads without a trace of feeling: "Ten thousand crowns, due on the thirtieth day. After the deadline fifty a day, and after seven days of delay we come for the property. Do you have property? You don't. Then mind the deadline."

collector_extend.text: "I don't extend. I take money and write numbers. Extensions come from Baldwin, and Baldwin gives them for a thousand crowns and a favour. If you want to talk to Baldwin, say so and I'll pass it on — for five crowns, because that's my work, not my kindness."

collector_threat.text: "I have no right. I have an entry in a ledger and thirty men who read that ledger. In this town that works better than law. One more sentence like that and I'll add ten crowns for insult. I have a separate column for it."

options.text: Let there be a column. Good day.

usurer_root.text: Rejne counts coins on the table without looking up. "I lend. Thirty percent a month, secured on goods or on a favour. I don't ask what for. I ask what you'll pay with if you don't pay."

options.text: How much will you lend against a pledge?
What happens when someone doesn't repay?
Tell me about yourself and this place.

usurer_200.text: "Two hundred today, two hundred sixty in a month. Security: your weapon, or your name in my ledger — which more people read than you think. Do you take it?"

usurer_pawn.text: "Against a pledge I give half the value of the thing, no bargaining. Iron, silver, relics — all the same, as long as it can be sold. The item sits in my chest until repayment. Don't repay and it sits with me forever, and you have the comfort of having 'sold' it."

usurer_consequences.text: "First a letter. Then a visit. Then something that can't be described in a letter. In this town I don't beat people — that's what the Knights are for, and I pay them. I simply make sure you stop being solvent for anyone else."

gambler_root.text: The player at the table doesn't look up. "The stake lies on the table, not in the mouth. You pay — you play. You win — you take. You lose — you sit on or stand up. You cheat — you leave through the window."

options.text: I'll play for a higher stake. (50)
Tell me about yourself and this place.

scribe_root.text: The scribe Urban puts down his quill. "Notebook: fourteen crowns, leather binding, twenty-four leaves. Quill and ink eight. Without a notebook a man remembers only what suits him, and that is the most expensive kind of forgetting."

options.text: Teach me to read. (30 crowns, one day)
Do you have any work for me?
Tell me about yourself and this place.

medic_root.text: The medic looks at your hands first, then at your face. "You're not bleeding. No. But you have the colour of a man who sleeps in his clothes and eats whatever falls into his hands. What troubles you — the body or the purse?"

options.text: Tell me about yourself and this place.

customs_root.text: Customs officer Bernard has a ledger and a stack of seals in front of him. "Everything that enters the town must be in the ledger. You are 'goods' too, until you have a pass. Say what you came for, the queue behind you is growing."

options.text: I want a harbour pass. (20 crowns)
I have a pass. Open the gate, please.
How much not to look in my purse?
You're missing twenty barrels of salt in your books.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

customs_bribe.text: Bernard glances around the room. "I didn't hear a question. But since you asked it: fifty crowns, and for an hour I have a great many papers to check. In that time the gate is sometimes... occupied with somebody else."

options.text: Too dear. I'll buy the pass.

customs_salt.text: Bernard closes the ledger. "Who told you that? ...No, don't answer. If you have proof — a crate, a seal, a name — you get thirty crowns from the coffers and my memory, which is sometimes useful. If you have only a rumour, you have a problem, because I dislike rumours about my own ledger."

options.text: I have a name: Idzi of the third pier.
I know nothing. I made it up.

customs_betray.text: "Idzi. I knew it. ...No, I didn't, but now I do. Thirty crowns and one warning: Idzi has friends in the harbour and you now have an enemy with a knife and a boat. Consider whether it was worth it."

guild_root.text: Zbylut of the Merchant Guild has soft hands and hard numbers. "The Guild pays for certainty, not for courage. You have goods — I buy. You have hands — I have a contract. You have a problem — I have a lawyer, but the lawyer costs more than the problem."

options.text: Do you have a caravan escort contract?
Orlik says the Knights take every tenth piece.
Rawicz needs the guild against the Raven.
Tell me about yourself and this place.
I'll come back when I have goods.

guild_escort.text: "I do. A cart with salt and iron goes out the road past the stone bridge the day after tomorrow at dawn. Eighty crowns for the day, twenty of it in advance. Condition: you come back with the cart. If the cart comes back without you, I pay your family, and that's dearer, so you'd rather come back."

options.text: I'll take the contract. (20 crowns advance)
I won't leave the town. I have thirty days.

guild_knights.text: "Orlik has a long tongue and a short memory of whom he tells what. Yes, they take. And yes, I reckon it will pass, because Baldwin is a merchant dressed as a knight and merchants don't burn what they live off. The question is what happens when it stops paying him. I don't know. And I don't want to know with witnesses present."

tanner_root.text: Oles wipes his hands on his apron and doesn't offer you his. "It stinks? It stinks. That's why my workshop is outside town and my prices are better than the guild's. I buy hides, I sell dressed leather. Say what you came with."

options.text: Teach me tanning. (55 crowns, one day)
Tell me about yourself and this place.

tanner_wolves.text: "I do. Forty-eight crowns for a whole one, twenty for a torn one. The wolves came down from the marshes because somebody burned their den — probably the same people who then complain that wolves are in town. Bring the pelt fresh, not dried on a stone."

fisher_root.text: Ewa has her hands in a net and the smile of someone who got up before dawn because she wanted to. "The fish were biting today. Buy, sell, or sit with me and learn where to cast — that costs less than a fish and lasts a lifetime."

options.text: I'll buy fish and a hook.
Teach me to fish. (40 crowns, one day)
Where is it quiet in this harbour?
Ambroży says he fishes better than you.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

fisher_quiet.text: "It's quiet behind the eastern wall, where there's a gap in the palisade. The guard doesn't walk there because they're afraid of the boggy ground. I'm telling you this because once you pulled my net out of the water — no, I'm joking. I'm telling you because you have the face of a man who'll go there anyway."

baker_root.text: Ignac has flour up to his elbows. "Bread is four crowns, because flour is dear — the miller says the river is low, and I say the miller plays dice. Are you buying or only sniffing?"

options.text: The miller plays dice? With whom?
Tell me about yourself and this place.

baker_dice.text: "With Pankracy, at night, at Hanna's. He loses flour, then he raises the price of grain, and finally I explain to the market women why a loaf costs four crowns. That's how the economy works, lad."

beggar_root.text: Lame Maciej holds out a hand but looks into your eyes, not at your purse. "I've sat here six years. I know who walks where and at what hour. A crown for a piece of news, two for one that hurts somebody."

options.text: Give me news for a crown.
What do you know about the Wild Knights?
Here's bread instead of a crown.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

beggar_rumor.text: "Marta from the west alley walks the market at night and nobody catches her, because the guard has short legs and long tongues. Idzi from the harbour has crates that aren't in any ledger. And Hanna at the inn has a chit for somebody's debt and hides it in the barrel behind the counter. Choose which piece of news is worth your crown."

options.text: All three. Here are two crowns more.

beggar_knights.text: "The Knights? They have a camp past the stone bridge, thirty men and twice as many horses. Every week they come for the levy, and Gwidon with his ledger walks the market reading names aloud so everybody hears. That isn't collecting money. That's theatre."

beggar_bread.text: Maciej takes the bread with both hands. "Bread is better than a crown, because I can't eat a crown. In return I'll tell you something free: don't sleep on the market after dark. Not because they'll rob you — they certainly will. Because the guard counts the sleepers and adds them to the vagrant list, and from the vagrant list you go to the stocks."

guard_root.text: The guard sets his spear upright. "Gate. A pass, or fifty crowns, or you turn back. I don't have a fourth option and I don't have all day."

options.text: Fifty crowns and you open it.
[Intimidate 4] Open it, or you'll regret it.

guard_intimidate.text: The guard steps back half a pace and looks at your hilt. "I'm not paid enough for this. Go through. But if anyone asks, I didn't see you and you didn't see me."

executioner_root.text: Baltazar sharpens his axe on a stone without breaking rhythm. "You're looking at the gallows, not at me. Everyone does. Ask, since you came."

options.text: How do you live with that work?
Tell me about yourself and this place.

executioner_tomorrow.text: "A boy, for a sack of grain. At dawn, on the market, so the stall women can see. Don't ask me whether it's just — ask those who write the sentences. I only carry them out and I eat from it."

executioner_life.text: "I live outside town, because nobody wants that neighbour. I eat at the inn by the door, because nobody wants that neighbour at the table. I earn three times what a guard does and I have no friends. That's the whole answer."

washer_root.text: Zofia wrings out a sheet. "You're as dirty as this harbour. Four crowns and you'll have a clean shirt in the morning. Or go to the bathhouse, they charge more but they have warm water."

options.text: What do people say at the washing?
Tell me about yourself and this place.

washer_gossip.text: "Washing is a second confession. From the stains you learn who drinks, who beats, who walks at night in the mud, and who has blood on his sleeve and says it's wine. This week two sleeves had 'wine'. I won't say whose, because I have children and I want to keep them."

stableboy_root.text: Pietrek holds a horse by the bridle and looks up at you. "Sir wants a horse? A horse costs eighty crowns and two sacks of oats a month. Or sir only wants to pat him — that's free, but don't approach from behind."

options.text: What do you charge for watching my things?
Tell me about yourself and this place.

stableboy_watch.text: "A crown a day. Nobody will touch it, because everyone knows it's mine. And if somebody does touch it, I'll tell you who — because I see everything here, I just pretend I don't."

nun_root.text: Sister Agnes puts down her book. "If you came to pray, the pew is free. If you came for help, we have bread for twelve and twelve places at the almshouse for the night. If you came out of curiosity — that's fine too, just don't make noise."

options.text: I'd like a place at the almshouse for the night.
Tell me about yourself and this place.

nun_book.text: "The chronicle of the island. The year fourteen twenty-eight — the one nobody wants to copy, because it has the abbey fire and a list of names in it. Father Teodor says the list is incomplete. I think it's complete, only somebody shortened it."

options.text: A list of names from the fire. I'll remember.

wiera_root.text: Wiera's hands smell of marsh and her eyes count how many days you have left. "You came from town and you stink like a man who sleeps too little. I have herbs, I have salves; I don't sell advice — I give it free, because you won't follow it anyway."

options.text: Teach me to recognise herbs. (65 crowns)
I have a wound that won't heal.
What grows in the marshes that can kill?
Gwidon sends me for forty crowns.
Widow Dorota's son has been coughing for three weeks.
Tell me about yourself and this place.
Thank you. I won't keep you.

wiera_wound.text: "Show me. ...Red edges, warm, smells sweet. That's not a wound any more, that's a guest. Salve is thirty-eight crowns, or wash it, dry it and don't move for two days — then it's free, but then you'll probably move. Choose between comfort and life, like everybody."

options.text: I'll wash it and keep still.

wiera_poison.text: "Spotted hemlock. It grows where yarrow grows and it looks like yarrow to anyone in a hurry. The difference: a hollow stem and spots. I sell it in a vial for ninety crowns and I don't ask what for. I only ask whether you know that there's no antidote, only time."

stranger_root.text: The man in the hood's shadow doesn't answer at once. "I don't know you. Go your way and I'll go mine, and we'll both have a good day."

options.text: Hand over the satchel at your belt.
I'm looking for Marta. Do you know her?

stranger_marta.text: "I know her. And I know what her satchel is worth. If you came to give it back, you're too late. If you came to take it — there are three of us and one of you. Count, don't talk."

teodor_ledger_start.text: “The Raven does not hold people with gold, but with memory. Every name from Vranov is in his ledger: who set the fire, who watched, who paid for silence. Mine is there too. As long as that book exists, nobody on this island is free. Idzi knows where the Raven keeps the copies. Go to him — just do not say I sent you.”

idzi_ledger.text: Idzi looks around before he answers. “Gwidon carries the ledger on him, but every week Bernard makes a copy for the council and keeps it in a chest in the customs office. By day Bernard sits at his desk counting other people's money. At night the office is empty, and that chest has a lock a child could open. You did not hear it from me.”

options.text: I did not hear it from you.

rawicz_ledger.text: Rawicz turns the pages slower and slower. “Twenty years I waited for someone to put this on my table. With it I can go to the council, but the council is more afraid than I am. I need the guild, the Church and the people from the suburb. If they stand behind me, we throw the Raven out of town in one night. Will you help?”

options.text: I will help. Let us begin.
Take the book, but I will not join the fight.

teodor_ledger.text: Teodor holds the book on his knees for a long time. “On Sunday I will read every name of the Vranov victims from the pulpit. Yours will be read as a witness, not an executioner. The Raven will not dare collect the full debt from a man the whole chapel stands behind — three thousand of your debt will be lost together with his good name.”

baldwin_ledger.text: Baldwin does not raise his voice, but his men step back. “I knew someone would carry it out one day. I thought Bernard, not you. Give it back and I will strike out half your debt. Take it to Rawicz or the priest — and you will have me as an enemy for the rest of your life, which will not be long.”

guild_overthrow.text: “The guild has paid the Raven a tenth for twenty years. Do you know how many crowns that is? I know it to the copper. I will stand behind Rawicz — but the guild does not take risks for free. Two hundred crowns for the journeymen's weapons, or a good name with us.”

options.text: The guild knows and trusts me.

teodor_bells.text: “Bells ring for fire, for funerals and for war. You ask for all three at once. ...Very well. When Rawicz gives the sign I will ring, and the people will come out to the square. But if innocent blood is spilled, I will walk to the Raven myself with your name.”

vagn_overthrow.text: “I fought for three kings and not one of them paid me. For Rawicz I can fight for free, because at least I know what for. But the suburb folk will follow someone they respect. Show me you are worth it, or buy them spears.”

options.text: People know I trained with you.
I will give a hundred crowns for spears.

rawicz_strike.text: “Do you hear it? The bell is ringing. Twelve of my men, forty journeymen under the guild banner and old Vagn with the suburb. The Raven has thirty in mail, but he also has a ledger with every one of us in it. Tonight we close it.”

idzi_ferry.text: “Everyone wants to disappear, not everyone can. The Grey Gull lies in the roads and asks no questions if her captain gets my token. The token costs six hundred crowns. The fishermen will row you out from the end of the middle pier — only at night and not in a storm, unless you want to meet the seabed in person.”

options.text: Too much. I will come back with the money.

idzi_relic.text: “Three hundred crowns and nobody will know it was you. Well, almost nobody — Teodor always knows.”

teodor_relic_back.text: Teodor takes the reliquary as if it were heavier than it is. “Saint Elenem comes home in the hands of a sellsword. The Lord has a sense of humour. From today the chapel doors are open to you at any hour — even when men with ravens on their cloaks come looking for you. Sanctuary is an old law, but the Raven still fears it.”

options.text: Let him return to the altar.

baldwin_oath_start.text: “Good. An oath is not sworn with words. Gwidon has a list — start with Wiera the herbwoman, forty crowns. Then the band on the eastern road: their chief steals from our wagons. Come back with blood on your sword, not a promise.”

wiera_debt.text: “Forty? For what? For breathing in their town? ...I have twenty and a salve for your wounds. Take what you want and go, before the children see.”

options.text: I will pay it for you from my own purse.

baldwin_oath.text: “On your knee. ...Repeat after me: ‘My name is in the ledger, and the ledger is my name.’ Rise, brother. Your debt has ceased to exist, because you have ceased to be a debtor. Now others owe you.”

options.text: My name is in the ledger.

halszka_root.text: Halszka does not look up from the loom. The shuttle flies back and forth, steady as breath. “If you came for cloth, I only have coarse linen. The good stuff goes to the guild, and the guild pays me half of what it charges.”

options.text: You look worried. Can I help?

halszka_about.text: “Halszka, daughter of a weaver from Vranov. Father taught me at the loom before he taught me to read. After the fire I sailed here with the loom in pieces and two knives in my sleeve. The loom came in handy. So did the knives.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

halszka_place.text: “Two looms, a spinning wheel and a bed I sleep in between one order and the next. The walls are thin — I hear every drunk in the alley. But the window faces east, and in the morning light you see every flaw in the weave.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

halszka_quest.text: “The guild ordered cloth from me for the council's cloaks. The deadline is in a week, and Oles the tanner sold all his wool to the Knights. I need three bundles of wool. Bring them and I will weave you a cloak that will see you through every winter on this island.”

klemens_root.text: Klemens holds a boot on the last and drives tacks from his mouth, one by one. He talks without spitting out a single one. “Sit if you have time. If you do not — leave your boots and come back tomorrow.”

options.text: What is the news in town?

klemens_about.text: “Thirty years I have made boots in this town. I made them for a mayor who is gone, for a council that is afraid, and for Knights who do not pay. Know the difference? The mayor wore out his soles, the council its heels, and the Knights — other people's doorsteps.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

klemens_rumor.text: “Someone walks between the warehouses at night in boots with iron heel-plates. In the whole town only three men wear those: Gwidon, Bernard of the customs and Rawicz himself. The tracks lead to the pier. I will say no more, because I like my hands.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

klemens_quest.text: “Lady Brygida wants doeskin slippers for her daughter's betrothal, and Oles has no hides because the hunters fear the forest. Bring me one deer hide — from the woods or from anyone — and I will pay honestly and resole your boots for free.”

dorota_root.text: Dorota spins by the window. In the corner, on a straw mattress, a boy sleeps wrapped in two blankets. He breathes heavily, with a whistle. “Speak quietly. And briefly, because every hour of spinning is bread for tomorrow.”

options.text: What is wrong with the boy?

dorota_about.text: “My husband was a cooper. He borrowed from the Raven for a new workshop, and the workshop burned a month later — strangely enough. The night before payment was due he left home and never returned. They say he drowned. I say someone helped him drown.”

options.text: The Raven has the same hook in me.
Let us talk about something else.

dorota_debt.text: Dorota looks up for the first time. “Then watch where you sleep. And never take a second loan from them to pay the first. That is how it starts.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

dorota_quest.text: “Coughing for three weeks. The barber wants more for bloodletting than I earn in a month, and Kuba's blood is pale enough already. Wiera the herbwoman knows what helps the lungs, but she is far, and I cannot leave him. If you would ask her what is needed...”

ambrozy_root.text: Ambroży mends a net with the speed of a man who has done it for sixty years. “What? The fish are gone, the stories are not. For a story you buy the beer. For a fish — you pay.”

options.text: What was the harbour like in the old days?

ambrozy_about.text: “I was born in a boat, in a storm, the year the king died — which king I do not remember, there were several. I sailed for herring to Gotland and for cod under the ice. I buried two wives, the third will outlive me, because she is forty years younger and wiser than me.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

ambrozy_place.text: “Once the Wild Knights were the coast watch. They took fish from us and in return burned the pirates' boats. An honest trade. Then came the plague, then the fire, then the Raven, and suddenly they only defend us from ourselves — for a tenth.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

ambrozy_quest.text: “Ewa from the eastern pier says she fishes better than me. I say she is young and foolish. A bet for a barrel of beer: bring me two cod caught with your own hand, and I will show her that even a stranger with my advice catches more than she does.”

options.text: I have no time for bets.

brygida_root.text: Brygida measures you from boots to brow, as if pricing goods. “I receive neither beggars nor suitors. If you are one of them — the door is behind you.”

options.text: What do you know of the Wild Knights?

brygida_about.text: “Brygida, widow of Henryk, who brought pepper, saffron and nutmeg to this island. Half the town ate only what he brought, and nobody remembers his name. I remember. And I count.”

options.text: May I help you with something?
Let us talk about something else.

brygida_help.text: The corners of her mouth twitch. “Perhaps. Bring me good news one day and I will remember your name. I rarely do.”

brygida_place.text: “Henryk bought it from a customs officer's widow for three chests of cinnamon. The sofa came from Bruges, the wardrobe from Lübeck, and the rug — from a place whose name I cannot pronounce. Everything here is from far away, except me. I am from here, and that worries me most.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

brygida_knights.text: Brygida is silent for a long time. “Henryk founded that brotherhood with six others. They were to defend the coast, not collect debts. When he died, Baldwin came to the funeral and promised me a pension for life. I take it because I am a coward. Every coin smells of smoke from Vranov.”

jas_root.text: Jaś bounces on his toes to see your sword better. “Sir knight! Have you ever killed a dragon? A wolf? A man? Mum says I must not ask, but Mum is not here.”

options.text: Here is a copper. Off home with you.

jas_about.text: “I am Jaś, son of Margaret who sells eggs. Dad was a sailor and sailed to Lübeck when I was three. When I grow up I will be a knight and sail to find him. A real knight, not the Raven's. The Raven's men kick dogs.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

jas_rumor.text: “I know! Master Gwidon gave me a letter for the customs man yesterday. It was heavy and it jingled. And the reeve of Brzezina comes to the Raven every Friday and goes home crying. And in the eastern forest there are wolves bigger than horses. Kinga with the sheep says so. Kinga never lies, only sometimes.”

options.text: Here is a copper for the news.
Let us talk about something else.

walenty_root.text: Walenty leans on the reeve's staff — worn smooth by the hands of three generations. “Welcome to Brzezina. Forty hearths, a mill, a chapel and a forest that takes someone from us every year. What are you looking for so far from the harbour?”

options.text: You said the forest takes people?

walenty_place.text: “Brzezina has stood here since before there was a town on the island. Rye, oats, flax, a few sheep. Bartosz grinds, Urszula heals, the priest comes from town once a month if the road is dry. We pay tribute to the Raven in grain, the tithe to the Church in grain, and the town tax — also in grain. What remains is enough not to die.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

walenty_about.text: “My grandfather and father were reeves. I am the first who has to choose whose children will go hungry this winter — ours or the Raven's. I choose every day. Not always well.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

walenty_wolves.text: “The pack from the forest killed four of our sheep this month and the village dog. Yesterday Kinga saw them by the pens in broad daylight. The Knights promised to send men — they have been promising for half a year. Kill three wolves from that pack and the village will pay you a hundred and twenty crowns. We have been saving since spring.”

options.text: I will deal with the pack.

bartosz_root.text: Bartosz brushes the flour off his hands and offers you one — white, heavy, calloused from sacks. “The mill stands still, but my mouth works. Speak.”

options.text: What is wrong with the mill?

bartosz_about.text: “A miller in the fourth generation. Grandfather said a miller must be part thief, part confessor and part carpenter. A thief I am by office, a confessor by habit — people talk by the millstones — and a carpenter, as you can see, a poor one.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

bartosz_quest.text: “The spring flood tore two paddles off the wheel and broke the shaft. Without the mill the village must haul grain to town, and the guild millers there take a third. I need two handfuls of nails from Orlik the smith and two oak planks from the guild house. I cannot go myself — the Raven knows I owe him for the millstones.”

options.text: I will bring nails and planks.

jadwiga_root.text: Jadwiga stands on the threshold of the hut, staring into the forest as if the forest could answer. “Maciek left five days ago. He took his axe and bread for one day.”

options.text: I will help you look for him.

jadwiga_about.text: “My husband. A woodcutter. Red-haired, tall, laughs so the birds fly off. He cuts timber for the mill and for Brzezina, and in winter for the town. He never slept in the forest. Never.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

jadwiga_quest.text: “Błażej, the hunter from the northern lodge, knows every path in this forest. But when I asked him, he looked away. He knows something. Go to him. He will tell me nothing, maybe he will tell you.”

jadwiga_cap.text: Jadwiga takes the cap and turns it in her fingers for a long time. She does not cry. “A boar. I thought so. I would rather a boar than the Knights — at least a boar does not lie that it was an accident.” She brings Maciek's axe from the hut. “Take it. It is no use to me anymore, and even less to him.”

blazej_root.text: Błażej does not stop skinning the hare. The knife moves fast and clean. “The forest does not like strangers, nor do I. But at least you walk quieter than the town folk.”

options.text: Jadwiga is looking for her husband. Do you know anything?

blazej_about.text: “I was huntsman to the lord of Vranov. After the fire the lord left, and I was left with a bow and no lord. Now I hunt for myself and for anyone who pays. The Knights say the forest is theirs because they wrote it in the ledger. The animals do not know that yet.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

blazej_place.text: “In the north pines and my lodge. In the middle old oaks — that is where the boars are, avoid them at dusk. In the south the woodcutters' clearing and the stream where wolves drink at dawn. To the east Brzezina. And beyond Brzezina only the sea and the old graveyard by the chapel, where Urszula says something haunts. Urszula says many things.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

blazej_maciek.text: Błażej puts down the knife. “...Maciek set snares on the Knights' land, next to mine. Five days ago I heard a boar and a scream by the bloody clearing, to the south-east. I did not go. I was afraid I would find him alive and have to explain what I was doing there. Go there. But be careful — a boar that has killed a man once does not fear a second.”

options.text: I will go to the clearing.

blazej_quest.text: “Oles the tanner pays forty crowns per wolf pelt, but I do not go to town — there you must show the Knights' seal for every hide. You can. Bring Oles two wolf pelts from me... or your own. He will not ask where from.”

options.text: I will take the pelts to Oles.

kinga_root.text: Kinga holds her shepherd's crook with both hands and scans the field. “Spotty ran away. Again. Father will kill me, and if not Father, the wolves will eat her, and then Father will kill me.”

options.text: I will help you find the goat.

kinga_about.text: “Kinga, Szymon's daughter. I herd the whole village's sheep because nobody else wants to — too little pay, too many wolves. But I like it. In the pasture nobody tells me whom to marry.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

kinga_quest.text: “Really? Spotty always runs south, into the forest, where sweet grass grows by the old stones. She has a bell on her neck, you will hear her. Just watch out for wolves!”

kinga_goat.text: Kinga jumps for joy. “She is back! She ran in by herself, covered in burrs, and you have her bell! Father noticed nothing!” She presses a bundle into your hand. “Cheese. I made it myself. Do not tell anyone I am crying.”

urszula_root.text: Urszula sits on the bench before her hut, peeling roots with a knife thin as a leaf. “Sit. Do not be afraid, I do not bite — I have no teeth left.”

options.text: I found a coin in the grave.

urszula_about.text: “Seventy-four winters. As a girl I served at the abbey of Saint Elenem — I washed habits and listened to the monks sing. Then the abbey burned, the monks scattered, and I was left with what I had heard. Herbs, prayers and stories. Everything heals, if you believe.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

urszula_legend.text: “Elenem was a fisherman, like your Ambroży. When the plague came to the island, he sailed into a storm for medicine from the mainland. He returned after three days, dead, lashed to the mast — and in his boat was a sack of herbs that saved half the island. The monks made him a saint and the sack a relic. I think he was just a stubborn man. Saints usually are.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

urszula_quest.text: “In the old graveyard by the chapel there is a grave with no name. At night a light glows there. People say — a ghost. I say — a monk who fled the abbey fire with something he should not have taken, and died here, in Brzezina. Go there at night and dig beneath the stone. By day you will find nothing — by day someone from the village is always watching.”

options.text: I do not dig in graves.

urszula_coin.text: Urszula rubs the coin with her thumb until the image of a monk with a net appears beneath the dirt. “An abbey coin. They were minted only for pilgrims... and for those paid to keep quiet. That monk knew who set fire to the abbey, and took his payment to the grave. Now you know it was not lightning.”

piotr_root.text: Piotr drives his hoe into the soil and wipes his brow with his sleeve. “God bless. If you are from the Raven — you took the grain last week. If not — good, because I have nothing else.”

options.text: I will give you a hand in the field.

piotr_about.text: “Piotr, a farmer. Three fields of land, a wife, five children, three of them living. My father was a free peasant, I am free only in name — the rest is in the Raven's ledger.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

piotr_place.text: “The soil is good, but the sea wind flattens the grain every third year. Wolves take the sheep, boars root up the turnips. And town folk only come to take something. You are the first who asks how life is.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

scribe_letter.text: “The council is sending the reeve of Brzezina a letter about a new mill tax. Nobody wants to go, because there are wolves in the forest, and the reeve bites worse than wolves. Take him the letter and you will get twenty-five crowns from the council.”

wiera_child.text: “A whistling cough? Yarrow. Three bunches, steeped with honey, twice a day for a week. And keep the window open even in the cold — soul and lungs both need air. Yarrow grows in the meadows by the forest. I can also sell you some if you are in a hurry.”

fisher_ambrozy.text: Ewa laughs so hard the gulls fly off. “Ambroży fished better than me before I was born. Now he mostly catches stories. But do not tell him — the old man lives only for beating me.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

hanna_about2.text: Hanna wipes a mug that is already clean. “The Rusty Cat was my father-in-law's tavern. When my husband died in the fire, the council wanted to sell it for debts. I paid them off in two years, pouring beer for the men who burned my home. Each of them has a tally here. None of them knows I remember.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

orlik_about2.text: Orlik sets down his hammer and wipes the sweat. “The forge is a hundred years old. The anvil older still — it came from Nuremberg on a ship that sank in the harbour. My grandfather hauled it out of the water for three days. They say a forge without history forges without soul. Mine has soul. Payment is another matter.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

vagn_about2.text: Vagn leans on the training post. “This yard is all that is left of my old glory. A post, two swords, a shield with a crossbow hole in it and the stool I sit on when the knee refuses. I trained boys here who later died at the gate. Now I train men like you — so they do not die stupidly.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

idzi_about2.text: Idzi folds his arms. “Warehouse B? Officially salt, tar and rope. Unofficially — everything the customs man did not see. The harbour has two faces, friend: the one by day, with seals, and the one by night, with boats without lanterns. I work both shifts.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

rawicz_about2.text: Rawicz looks at the gate. “Twelve men for the whole town. Three drink, two take more from the Raven than I do, and one is deaf. The guardhouse leaks, the crossbows are older than the crossbowmen. But when someone screams at night, we come running. Almost always.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

teodor_about2.text: Teodor lights a candle from a candle. “Fishermen built this chapel from stones they pulled up in their nets. Every stone is a catch that did not feed a family. That is why it is so small — and why it is holy. The reliquary stood there, in the empty place by the altar.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

marta_about2.text: Marta shrugs. “The alley behind the bakery. Warm from the oven, and the baker pretends not to see me. I have a blanket, a knife and a treasure box. Better than the almshouse — there they count your spoons and your prayers.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

goslaw_about2.text: Gosław unrolls a map reverently. “This island has three maps: one for the council, one for the Raven and the true one. I drew them all. The eastern forest is larger than the council would like, and Brzezina smaller than the Raven says when he counts the tribute.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

baldwin_about2.text: Baldwin smiles coldly. “The room above the stable. It smells of horses, you can hear the tavern and see the square. From here I see every debtor who walks into Hanna's instead of mine. It is the best view on the island.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

scribe_about2.text: Zbylut adjusts his spectacles. “The chancery is the town's memory. Contracts, wills, verdicts, love letters — I write it all, for a fee. These drawers hold more secrets than Father Teodor's confessional. And better organised.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

medic_about2.text: Marcin washes his hands in a bowl of vinegar. “I shave, let blood, set bones and pull teeth. The bathhouse next door brings me customers — whoever washes sees what has grown on him. Last year I saved twenty people. Buried thirty. An honest tally for this trade.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

customs_about2.text: Bernard turns a page in the ledger. “Every sack that comes into the harbour passes through this room. Every one — officially. The council pays me for what I write down, the Raven for what I do not. An honest man would go mad here. I am doing fine.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

guild_about2.text: Rejne spreads his arms as if to embrace the whole guild house. “Cloth, salt, timber, grain. The guild holds prices so nobody starves or gets too rich. A beautiful theory. In practice we get rich and others starve.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

tanner_about2.text: Oles wipes his hands on his apron, which changes nothing. “The tannery stinks, I know. But somebody has to turn a cow into a boot and a wolf into a cloak. My vats run all the way to the stream. The water there is brown and the fish have left. They say it is my fault. They tell the truth.”

fisher_about2.text: Ewa nods toward the sea. “The eastern pier is my kingdom. Three boats, twenty nets and a smokehouse whose smoke you can see from the square. Fishers on this side leave before dawn and return after dark. The Knights do not rise that early, so at least in the mornings we are free.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

baker_about2.text: Grzegorz brushes flour off his apron. “I light the oven at three in the morning, the bread is out by five. By noon I have sold everything, in the afternoon I sleep. I have not seen a sunset in thirty years. But I know everyone in town by the bread they buy.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

collector_about2.text: Gwidon taps the black raven painted on his door. “People spit when they walk past this house. Let them spit. Spit does not wash away debt. The list is long, and I have good legs.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

usurer_about2.text: Mojsze smiles through the bars. “A pawnshop is the poor man's apothecary. They come in with a wedding ring and leave with bread. They come back with money — sometimes. I have a chest full of other people's memories here and I guard each as if it were mine.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

gambler_about2.text: “The table by the window has the best light — you see every die and every face. Sailors play here, guards, sometimes even the priest, though he pretends he is only watching. Dice know no ranks, friend. Only luck.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

beggar_about2.text: Jędrek scratches his stump. “The north gate is the best spot in town. Everyone coming in still has money. Everyone leaving has a bad conscience. I earn from both.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

executioner_about2.text: Wawrzyniec looks at the gallows like a carpenter at a table. “My house stands outside the walls because the town does not want a hangman inside. But when there is a sentence, everyone comes to watch. People love justice, as long as they need not carry it out.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

washer_about2.text: Zofia wrings a shirt as hard as if it were someone's neck. “The tubs by the stream. The water is cold, the lye bites your hands, but people talk while washing. I know whose shirt has blood on it, whose has perfume and whose has tavern vomit. The truth always comes out in the wash.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

stableboy_about2.text: Paweł strokes a horse's muzzle. “I sleep here, in the hay, between Greybeard and Chestnut. Warmth from horses is better than from a stove. Horses do not hit you or ask whose son you are.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

nun_about2.text: Sister Agnieszka straightens her veil. “The almshouse has twelve beds and always one too few. Old men, widows, orphans, shipwrecked sailors. We feed them with what we have and pray for the rest. Sometimes it helps. More often Hanna helps, sending leftovers from the tavern.”

options.text: Let us talk about something else.

wiera_about2.text: Wiera sniffs a bunch of dried herbs. “The marsh behind the tannery is the best apothecary on the island. Everything that heals grows there, and half of what kills. You only need to know which is which. Town folk do not. That is why they come to me — after dark, so the neighbours do not see.”
